;Armed conflicts and attacks 
*[[Sino-Indian border dispute]]
**[[2020 China–India skirmishes]]
***At least 20 [[Indian Army|Indian soldiers]] and an unknown number of [[People's Liberation Army Ground Force|Chinese soldiers]] have been killed in a clash in [[Ladakh]] in the disputed [[Kashmir|Kashmir region]], amid rising [[China–India relations|tensions between the two countries]]. Local media reported that the Indian soldiers were "beaten to death", and the Indian Army says no shots were fired. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53061476 (BBC News)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[list of heads of state of Mali|President]] [[Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta]] says that opposition leader [[Soumaïla Cissé]], who was [[kidnap]]ped in late March, is alive. Keïta said "we know who his captors are [...] And if it pleases God, he will come back soon". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/mali-keita-abducted-opposition-leader-soumaila-cisse-alive-200616191957695.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 boogaloo killings]]
**The alleged gunman in a fatal attack on [[Santa Cruz County, California|Santa Cruz County]] deputies is also charged with last month's [[murder (United States law)|murder]] of a [[Federal Protective Service (United States)|Federal Protective Service]] officer in [[Oakland, California]]. A second man is also charged as an accomplice. Both men had ties to the [[far-right politics in the United States|far-right]] [[boogaloo movement]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/airman-charged-killing-federal-officer-during-george-floyd-protests-california-n1231187 (NBC News)]

;Business and economy
*The [[World Trade Organization]] rules that the [[Government of Saudi Arabia|Saudi government]] violated [[Qatar]]’s intellectual property rights by promoting the [[Pirate television|pirate]] TV station [[beoutQ]], which aired Qatari programs like [[beIN Sports (Middle East TV network)|beIN Sports]] after [[Saudi Arabia]] and several other [[Middle East]]ern countries cut ties with the Kingdom during the [[Qatar diplomatic crisis]]. The Qatari Communications Minister applauds the decision, while Saudi Arabia denies any involvement. [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/saudi-state-beoutq-piracy-tv-operation-wto-ruling-200616074321753.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[Beijing]] closes all schools, locks down several residential estates and imposes a partial travel ban, urging residents not to leave the city, after 27 more [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases are confirmed in the city, bringing the total to 106 new cases in the last five days. The new outbreak is linked to the [[Xinfadi Market]]. [http://www.thenations.co.uk/news/beijing-imposes-partial-travel-ban-closes-schools-over-new-coronavirus-outbreak/ (''The Nations'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Ministry of Health]] reports a record 34,918 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 1,282 more deaths in the last 24 hours. Despite the record daily rise, [[Chief of Staff of the Presidency (Brazil)|Chief of Staff of the Presidency]] [[Walter Souza Braga Netto]] says the virus is now under control. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronvirus-brazil/brazil-sees-record-daily-coronavirus-cases-official-says-outbreak-under-control-idUSKBN23N3EE (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras]]
***[[President of Honduras|President]] [[Juan Orlando Hernández]] says that he, his wife, and their aides have been diagnosed with COVID-19. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/honduran-president-diagnosed-with-covid-19-12843896 (CNA)]
**The total cases surpass eight million worldwide. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/world/419126/covid-19-more-than-8-million-cases-worldwide (RNZ)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**The [[General Staff Department of the Korean People's Army]] says they are on "high alert" and are looking at plans to mobilize [[Korean People's Army Ground Force|the army]] into the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|demilitarized zone]], in response to [[North Korean defectors|defector groups]]  in [[South Korea]] sending propaganda material across [[Military Demarcation Line|the border]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53059437 (BBC News)]
**[[North Korea]] blows up the four-storey [[Inter-Korean Liaison Office]] in the [[Kaesong Industrial Region]], according to South Korean authorities. [[Kim Yo-jong]], the sister of [[List of leaders of North Korea|Supreme Leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]], had earlier threatened to destroy the "useless" building. A neighbouring apartment complex used by South Korean officials appears to have partially collapsed in the explosion. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200616008300325 (Yonhap)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/south-korea-north-blew-liaison-office-tensions-rise-200616071045580.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Chinese intelligence activity abroad]], [[Sino-Russian relations since 1991]]
**Russian investigators accuse Valery Mitko, President of Arctic Academy of Sciences in St. Petersburg and one of the country's leading Arctic researchers, "of treason" after alleging that he gave a document containing state secrets to Chinese intelligence in early 2018 at China's Dalian Maritime University, where he was a visiting professor. Mitko and his lawyer Ivan Pavlov deny any wrongdoing and say that all the materials were openly available. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/17/europe/russia-china-spying-allegation-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[Police reform in the United States]]
**In the aftermath of the [[killing of George Floyd]] last month, [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an executive order limiting the use of [[Chokehold#Use in law enforcement (lateral vascular neck restraint)|police chokeholds]], except in cases where “deadly force is allowed by law”. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/06/16/trump-signs-executive-order-urging-police-reform-says-cops-need-more-funding.html (CNBC)]
*[[Moldova]] asks the U.S. to extradite businessman [[Vladimir Plahotniuc]] after accusing him of "involvement in the theft of $1 billion from banks in 2014–2015". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-moldova-tycoon-usa/moldova-asks-u-s-to-extradite-tycoon-plahotniuc-over-1-billion-theft-idUSKBN23N2XT?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]] CEO [[William D. Johnson (CEO)|Bill Johnson]] pleads guilty on behalf of his company to 84 counts of felony involuntary manslaughter in the [[Camp Fire (2018)|2018 Camp Fire]], the deadliest wildfire in [[California]]'s history, as well as one felony count of unlawfully starting a fire. PG&E will pay a maximum fine of [[United States dollar|US$]]3.5 million, as well as an additional US$500,000 for the cost of investigations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/pge-pleads-guilty-84-deaths-2018-california-wildfire-200616183543588.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.sacbee.com/news/california/fires/article243571597.html ''(The Sacramento Bee'')]
*The [[Indonesian National Police]] says that they have arrested Russ Medlin, an American fugitive wanted at home in connection with a $700 million [[cryptocurrency]] scam, on local [[Child prostitution|teenage sex]] charges. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/16/indonesia-arrests-us-fraud-fugitive-on-local-sex-charges.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Tanzanian general election]]
**[[President of Tanzania|President]] [[John Magufuli]] dissolves [[Parliament of Tanzania|parliament]] ahead of the election. In the decision, he highlights his [[Government of Tanzania|government]]'s achievements, citing "expanding infrastructure such as roads, electricity generation and reforming the mining sector". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tanzania-politics/tanzanian-president-magufuli-dissolves-parliament-before-vote-touts-development-record-idUSKBN23N23P?il=0 (Reuters)]
